# Roadmap and delivery

Use this skill when turning approved opportunities into transformation
initiatives and measuring delivery. The roadmap should answer what the client
should do, and in what order; it is not another project-management suite.

Place opportunities in the four Trion phases:

| Phase | Timing |
| --- | --- |
| Simplify | 0-3 months |
| Connect | 3-6 months |
| Optimise | 6-12 months |
| Scale | 12+ months |

The primary roadmap view should make initiative, phase, timing, priority,
dependencies, and expected outcome clear. An initiative retains its originating
opportunity context and can model scope, owner, actions, milestones,
dependencies, status, cost, expected benefits, actual benefits, risks,
decisions, and outcomes, but detailed delivery tracking should not dominate the
workbench.

Keep expected benefits separate from realised benefits and distinguish plans
from evidence of impact. Preserve links from initiative to opportunity,
engagement, actions, and outputs. Prefer context, sequencing, dependencies,
and measurable outcomes over task volume, resource allocation, team workload,
or enterprise scheduling behaviour.
